 From pregame until the end of the game and the clock reads 00:00, live updates (refreshed frequently) as Baylor goes on the road to take on Kansas. Brad Teague | Share on Facebook Share on X Add us as a preferred source IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In this story:
 Baylor Bears Lawrence, Kansas, is where the Bears find themselves this week, taking to the road in hopes of forgetting the sting from the loss at home to TCU last week . The Jayhawks of Kansas are playing host this week , and are also coming off of a loss last week to their rival, KSU. Baylor comes into the game favored and looking to win their 15th straight against the Jayhawks, but this is Kansas' homecoming game and they aren't going to go down without a fight.

 Two Minutes Remain in the Game
--> Two Minutes Remain in the Game
 Kansas is trailing Baylor 24-19, but has the ball with two minutes left in the game. A field goal won't win this game, the Jayhawks need a touchdown. Baylor will have to clamp down tightly and not allow that to happen. Now would be the optimal time for the Bears defense to force a turnover and seal this game off from Kansas.

 Clock Management and Play Calling Have me Scratching my Head. 
--> Clock Management and Play Calling Have me Scratching my Head. 
 Rhett nails one from 42 ✅
Baylor 24, Kansas 19 | 2:40 4Q #SicEm pic.twitter.com/VM2FMDSF98 
— Baylor Football (@BUFootball) October 24, 2026 Baylor would run a few plays, take minimal time off of the clock, and ultimately kick a 42 yard field goal to extend their lead to 24-19. Snapping the ball with almost 20 seconds on the game clock when you have the lead is confusing, false start penalties to stop the clock and move the offense backwards isn't any better, and an incompletion with nobody in the vicinity is just baffling.

--> 4 Straight Running Plays Turn the Ball Over on Downs and Back to Baylor Possession

— Baylor Football (@BUFootball) October 24, 2026 In 4-down mode, Kansas came out after the interception and ran the ball on four straight downs, failing to make ten yards. This is the strength of the Baylor defense and the potential momentum they need to hold on and win this game.

 Tip Drill INT
--> Tip Drill INT
 An overthrow for the intended Freeman, a tip, and a second tip would see Lagway's 3rd down pass end up intercepted by Kansas. I don't blame Lagway entirely, but he's certainly not absolved from responsibility on this one; he definitely tried to squeeze the pass in there too tightly. However, it hit the hands of the receiver, so I'm torn on how to judge this one. One thing is for certain though, Baylor's offense is still a mess.

--> 34 Yard Touchdown on 4th Down

— Baylor Football (@BUFootball) October 24, 2026 With more confidence in Baylor's defense than it's offense, I'm not a big fan of how well Kansas is able to move the ball down the field. The Bears have had success in minimalizing damage by the Kansas offense, but as the 4th quarter starts, it's only a two possession game as Baylor leads 21-10. Kansas will be starting the 4th quarter with a 4th down play where they will most likely be attempting the conversion.

--> Illegal Substitution Penalty on Kansas Cancels out Ugly Lagway Sack

Baylor 21, Kansas 10 | 6:41 3Q #SicEm pic.twitter.com/pFZSS48uYA 
— Baylor Football (@BUFootball) October 24, 2026 A DJ Lagway sack that saw Lagway lose 11 yards on the play was canceled out by an illegal substitution penalty. What was set to be a 3rd and very long was now a 2nd and 11. Lagway would then run up the middle to bring it to a 3rd and short, a handoff would then gain the first down.

Kyland Reed would explode through the line to sack Marshall on 2nd down to bring up 3rd and 23. A short completion later would see the field goal unit come out for a successful 40 yard field goal attempt. Baylor leads 14-10

 2nd Quarter Thoughts
--> 2nd Quarter Thoughts
 Second half starts now 👊 pic.twitter.com/MsWiMGmqzN 
— Baylor Football (@BUFootball) October 24, 2026 Baylor can absolutely win this game, but unless they can begin to assert some kind of dominance on offense the Bears can also lose this game just as easily. Baylor is trailing in overall plays run to Kansas 46-35, and only held the ball for 10:20 the entire first half. A few passes by Kansas could have easily have been touchdowns, one overthrown and one that just couldn't be held onto, couple that with the Jayhawks 49 yard field goal that was pushed wide right, Baylor is lucky for the game to only be tied at 7 at this point.

 Kansas' Isaiah Marshall was sacked by Mitchell on first down on a drive that would ultimately end in a three-and-out. Baylor would run a few plays before the end of the half, but being safe and conservative in nature, the Bears would head into the half tied at 7 with the Jayhawks

 2 Minutes Until Halftime
--> 2 Minutes Until Halftime
 A Lagway pass to Livingston would gain 27 yards right before the two-minute mark before halftime. A sack for a six yard loss, and a screen for no gain would have the Bears staring down a three-and-out on 3rd and 17 with 1:32 to go before the half. A bad pass without a Baylor receiver even in the area. By far the worst drive that the Bears have had all game.

Twice though on this drive Kansas has missed guaranteed touchdown passes (one an overthrow, one just couldn't be wrangled in for a catch). Third time was the charm on this drive though as the pass attempt to convert falls incomplete, nearly intercepted.

Kick the field goal, take the points, and move from there. A failure on 4th down just gives the ball back to Kansas and leaves the game tied at 7 apiece.

 Kansas Misses 49 Yard Field Goal, Despite Success Running the Ball
--> Kansas Misses 49 Yard Field Goal, Despite Success Running the Ball
 SLUG + GP 😤💪😤 pic.twitter.com/cUBe5VFtXr 
— Baylor Football (@BUFootball) October 24, 2026 Kansas is able to move the ball on the ground. Not for large chunks and massive plays, but the Jayhawks are having success running against the Bears offense. Up the middle of the Baylor defense seems to be a slight soft spot against the run, but the Bears were able to hold firm and not only prevent Kansas from gaining a first down, but when Kansas would try to kick a 49 yarder, it would be pushed just right and "no good."
 Game remains tied at 7

 1st Quarter Thoughts
--> 1st Quarter Thoughts
 Knotted up after 1️⃣ pic.twitter.com/8MTUfRhgRt 
— Baylor Football (@BUFootball) October 24, 2026 After Kansas would see their next drive end in a punt, Baylor would end the 1st quarter in control of the ball. Lagway has shown a willingness to run if need be, and that's huge for the Bears, but the running game hasn't yet established itself yet this game. The Baylor defense seems to be honing in on their usual standard of pressuring the quarterback as well as blanketing the opposing wide receivers. Plenty of game left to play, but this one is shaping up into what could be a tightly contested game between the two games.

However, just a few plays later, a 22 yard pass to the tight end Carson Bruhn wouldn't have any penalties. An extra point kick later, and just like that, Baylor trails Kansas 7-0.

 Baylor's Opening Drive : Michael Turner started as running back and would get a few carries, some short gains and one that had some momentum and gained a first down after a decent gain. DJ Lagway would connect with Gavin Freeman for the first time in the game. Lagway would even run his first designed QB run since the Auburn game. Coming up short of the first down though on third down, Baylor would leave the offense on the field for 4th down. After the pass was thrown incomplete, Baylor has turned the ball over on downs.
